hook: If you understand anxiety perfectly well in theory but still can't stop it when it hits — this is specifically for you.
topic: The gap between knowing and doing under nervous system activation
body:
**If you understand anxiety perfectly well in theory but still can't stop it when it hits — this is specifically for you.**

You've read the explanations. You know about the amygdala. You've heard about breathing. You could probably explain all of this to someone else.

And then it happens, and you can't access any of it.

This is not an intelligence failure. When your threat response is fully activated, your access to the prefrontal cortex — the part of your brain where all that knowledge lives — is genuinely, physiologically reduced. You are not being weak. You are operating a system that has deliberately routed around higher-order thinking because it believes there isn't time for it.

Understanding anxiety and having an automatic, drilled response to anxiety are two completely different cognitive states. The knowledge doesn't help in the moment because it's stored in the wrong part of the brain for that moment.

What helps is a response that is so simple and so practised that it doesn't require you to think. Three steps. Body first. Sensory anchor second. Redirect third.

The protocol is free — link in my bio.
